discovery.title: Meta unveils new AI models built for agents that take action
discovery.summary: Meta introduced Muse Wonder and Muse Wonder Full, models it says are designed for complex personal and professional agent tasks, including coding and handling documents such as leases or insurance claims.
discovery.why_it_matters: AI tools moving from answering questions to acting across tasks could alter who does routine professional work—and how privacy, oversight, and mistakes are managed.

discovery.title: Newly described bacterial defense system links viral immunity and telomerase-like chemistry
discovery.summary: Columbia researchers reported a bacterial antiviral defense system called DRT10 that uses reverse transcription to make DNA, rather than cutting DNA as CRISPR does. The study also points to a relationship with telomerase-like mechanisms.
discovery.why_it_matters: The work may illuminate the evolution of genome machinery and could inspire future biotechnology, although applications such as gene editing remain speculative.

discovery.title: Antarctic sea ice reaches its third-lowest winter peak
discovery.summary: NASA and the National Snow and Ice Data Center estimate that Antarctic sea ice peaked on September 14 at 17.59 million square kilometers, the third-lowest maximum in satellite records.
discovery.why_it_matters: The observation adds to a period of generally low Antarctic ice, but scientists caution that year-to-year variation makes the long-term meaning uncertain.

discovery.title: A DNA “typewriter” traces more than a million embryonic cell histories
discovery.summary: Researchers used sequential DNA marks to reconstruct relationships among about 1.28 million profiled cells from a developing mouse embryo, from its first division to late organ development.
discovery.why_it_matters: Mapping how cells arise and specialize could give researchers new ways to study development and disease, while the demonstrated work remains in mice rather than a clinical tool.

discovery.title: Small Greek island moves toward electricity powered mainly by renewables
discovery.summary: A report published October 12 says Agios Efstratios has gone from fossil-fuel reliance to producing more than 90% of its electricity from renewable sources over ten months through an EU-supported project.
discovery.why_it_matters: The island’s experience could offer lessons for remote communities seeking to reduce reliance on imported fuels, though its scale and local conditions may not transfer directly elsewhere.
